subject: Clarifying hosted API latency commitments and operational safeguards
messages:
From: Arman Patel <arman@finstream.io>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.example>
Cc: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@finstream.io>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API latency targets — request for clarity

Hi Mina —

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we progress with procurement, our engineering and SRE teams need a clear statement on latency commitments for the hosted API. Specifically:

- What are the p50 and p95 latency targets we can expect under your standard "Production Hosted" tier?
- How do you measure those percentiles (measurement window length, sampling cadence)?
- What protections do you offer during brief regional bursts or maintenance (e.g., temporary grace periods, carveouts)?

We have a strict internal SLA to our end customers and want to avoid surprises. Can you share a short operational summary and any suggested wording we should include in our contract?

Appreciate it —
Arman
Sr. Platform Eng, Finstream

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.example>
To: Arman Patel <arman@finstream.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 12:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency targets — request for clarity

Arman —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: our Production Hosted tier target is p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 320ms for standard text-generation calls under our reference request profile. Below are the operational details and recommended contract wording. I copied Karthik and Ben to help with commercial language and evidence we can provide during onboarding.

Operational notes (summary):
- Measurement: rolling 24-hour measurement window computed at 1-minute resolution. Percentiles are calculated on successful response latencies (server-side processing + network edge egress). We exclude very short-lived health-check and admin calls.
- Sampling: every request to the endpoint is included; no downsampling for production customers.
- Burst handling: short regional bursts (under 5 minutes) are expected; we provide automatic traffic shaping and short-lived slower responses rather than failed requests. For sustained bursts we offer traffic rerouting and can temporarily provision additional dedicated capacity via our burst plan.
- Grace policy: we provide a 48-hour transient carveout for verified infrastructure maintenance events or cloud-provider incidents if evidence is supplied.

Suggested contract clause (plain language):
"Redwood Inference will maintain, for the hosted Production tier, a rolling p50 latency of at most 60 milliseconds and a rolling p95 latency of at most 320 milliseconds, measured over a 24-hour window at 1-minute resolution on successful API responses. Temporary grace periods for verified provider incidents (up to 48 hours) will be applied per the parties' incident evidence process."

I can attach a short evidence pack (sample measurement export + a brief explainer). Karthik / Ben — please add any commercial notes.

Best,
Mina
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
To: Arman Patel <arman@finstream.io>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.example>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency targets — request for clarity

Hi Arman —

A couple of commercial points to help your procurement team: 
- Standard contractual measurement window is 24 hours; customers can request 7-day aggregated reporting for trending but it does not change objective short-term commitments.
- For customers requiring a tighter p95 (e.g., p95 <= 250ms), we offer a Dedicated capacity option (reserved GPUs) with financial commitment; we can scope this in the SOW if needed.
- If you need a limited-time temporary relaxation (for example during a data migration cutover), we can include a one-off SLO reprofiling clause (up to 14 days) with agreed evidence and a credit schedule.

I'll attach a redlined SLA draft and a CSV sample showing how we compute percentiles.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: finstream-sla-draft-v2.pdf, slo-measurement-sample.csv

On Wed, Aug 3, 2026 at 10:05 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example> wrote:
> Hi Arman —
> 
> A couple of commercial points to help your procurement team: 
> - Standard contractual measurement window is 24 hours; customers can request 7-day aggregated reporting for trending but it does not change objective short-term commitments.
> - For customers requiring a tighter p95 (e.g., p95 <= 250ms), we offer a Dedicated capacity option (reserved GPUs) with financial commitment; we can scope this in the SOW if needed.
> - If you need a limited-time temporary relaxation (for example during a data migration cutover), we can include a one-off SLO reprofiling clause (up to 14 days) with agreed evidence and a credit schedule.

Thanks for the clarity. Two follow-ups from our side: 
1) What qualifies as acceptable "evidence" for a 48-hour grace? Is a cloud provider incident ticket + our incident timeline enough, or do you require telemetry exports?
2) Our security team wants to confirm that measurement excludes any responses served by cached pre-warm paths (we rely on consistent tail latency).

Can you confirm both?

—Jamie
Head of Procurement, Finstream

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
To: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@finstream.io>, Arman Patel <arman@finstream.io>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.example>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency targets — request for clarity

Jamie / Arman —

Quick answers:
1) Evidence for a transient grace: cloud provider incident ticket + our cross-check of region-level telemetry is sufficient. If the customer supplies a post-incident timeline and a HubSpot ticket reference, we will accept that and apply the 48-hour carveout. We typically request request/response telemetry (aggregated CSV like the sample we attached) only if there is a dispute about scope.
2) Measurement exclusion: cached pre-warm responses (prefix KV-cache hits that serve warm responses) are excluded from p50/p95 computation for the contractual measurement; we only include responses that traverse the standard runtime path. We do retain detailed cache hit metrics for transparency and can provide a weekly cache-effectiveness report on request.

Next steps: I'll push the redlined SLA to the Google doc (link below). If this covers your needs, Karthik and I can coordinate a short procurement call to finalize the SOW and any Dedicated capacity quotes.

Doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1XqFinstream-slo-notes

Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
